40 unique synthetic strings: ten contain the stub emergency trigger, thirty use
its review branch. Numbered cases are artificial, never patient data. Labels assert
a programming contract, not clinical correctness. Benchmark submits all 40 cold
inputs, then cases 0–29 twice (100 total). With no expiry/eviction, 60 hits / 100 =
60%; gate 55% permits at most five lost hits. Short wording/negation tests verify
keys remain distinct; the stub still mishandles negation and is not clinically safe.
